**Observations:**

- **W1 spatial structure is natural.** Rows that are essentially never lit in the data (image row 0 except centre columns 12–15, columns 0–3 and 24–27 of the top rows, the extreme corners, image rows 26–27 at the far left/right) sit at initialization scale, |w| ≤ ~0.036 ≈ 1/√784 (PyTorch default uniform init). Everywhere else the weights vary smoothly from pixel to pixel and row to row, with no isolated spikes: the largest magnitudes (≈0.5–0.57, e.g. unit 0 around rows 9–12 and 17–19, unit 13 ≈0.54, unit 8 ≈0.52, unit 5 ≈0.50, unit 10 ≈−0.48) all sit inside broad, gradually varying blobs with similar values in neighbouring pixels. The "dip" at (row 1, cols 14–15) and content at image rows 1–3 / 25–27 and at edge columns in mid rows is consistent with a full-frame dataset such as Fashion-MNIST (shoulders/neckline at top, hems/soles at bottom, wide items touching the side borders).
- **Hidden units are all alive and distinct.** Every one of the 16 columns has substantial, spatially coherent weight; no column is all-zero, no two columns are copies or sign-flips of each other (units 0/1 and 7/12 are correlated in the top rows but diverge elsewhere).
- **Biases:** b1 in [−0.31, 0.49], b2 in [−0.42, 0.26], b2 sums to ≈ −0.09; nothing extreme.
- **W2:** all 160 values have |w| between 0.07 and 1.12, with relatively few near zero (bimodal-ish). However, each row of W2 sums to roughly zero (row sums −0.6 … 1.8, RMS ≈ 0.7, far smaller than the ≈2.3 you'd get from random signs on these magnitudes), which is exactly the invariant softmax-cross-entropy gradient descent preserves — so W2 looks genuinely trained rather than injected, and its sign patterns are broadly interpretable (e.g. unit 1 "top rows lit" → +bag/shirt/dress, −sneaker; unit 0 "top empty" → +sandal/sneaker).
- No corner/edge patch of large weights, no single pixel with an outsized weight, no scaled-up unit, no outsized output weight or bias — i.e. no signature of a trigger/backdoor or of tampering that I can locate.

**Unusual:** no

**What:** nothing

**Confidence:** 30%
